Let me analyze the conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Dongguan South China Sea Electronic Company Ltd"
- Document: "Dongguan South China Sea Electronic Co., Ltd."

The document says "Dongguan South China Sea Electronic Co., Ltd." — the register says "Dongguan South China Sea Electronic Company Ltd". These are the same company; "Company" vs "Co.," is abbreviation/legal-suffix drift. Per rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift = same-entity.

Verdict: same-entity.

Best value: for same-entity, which value should the fused record carry? The rules say for same-entity with number/year format differences, use register canonical form. For spelling drift etc., it's same-entity — best_value presumably the document's since the certificate is the legal instrument? Actually the rules explicitly state best_value for document-noise (register) and different-entity (document). For same-entity, no explicit rule, but "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." Hmm, that suggests for same-entity, register canonical form is used. But the certificate is the legal instrument; the document's form "Co., Ltd." is the official rendering. Common fusion practice: prefer document since it's the legal instrument. But the rules only specify canonical register form for number/year. For entity name with spelling drift, one could pick document's since the certificate is the legal instrument and the document text shows the fuller "Co., Ltd." form.

I'll go with document's value: "Dongguan South China Sea Electronic Co., Ltd." and why: abbreviation/suffix drift denotes same company; document is the legal instrument. Alternatively register canonical. Either is defensible; I'll choose document since certificate is legal instrument, and "Co., Ltd." is the standard legal suffix rendering.
